title: Exceptional inverse image on a closed affine-space chart
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and put $A=\mathcal O_E/t^n$ for a uniformizer $t$ and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ be affine open subschemes such that $f(U)\subseteq V$. Suppose $i:U\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^r_V$ is a closed immersion, $r\geq0$, and $fu=v\pi i$, where $\pi:P\to V$ is the projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $f_A^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint to $Rf_{!,A}=Rg_{*,A}j_!$ for a compactification $f=gj$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Use ordinary etale module derived categories, bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. There is a canonical counit-preserving natural isomorphism on the entire ordinary derived categories
$$u^*f_A^\times L\simeq Ri_A^!\bigl(\pi^*v^*L(r)[2r]\bigr),$$
where $Ri_A^!$ is the right adjoint of the exact closed pushforward [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and $(r)$ is the ordinary etale Tate twist of [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]. For every bounded constructible finite-Tor $L$ on $Y$, the expression on the right is bounded constructible and has finite Tor amplitude on $U$. No boundedness of $f_A^\times L$ is assumed in forming the isomorphism.

source.place: Locality and Charts; arbitrary-map closed affine chart supplement to thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity Steps 1–2; extraction of old item Steps 5–6

proof.text: First check the domains of the operations. The coefficient datum makes $A$ finite. In the DVR $\mathcal O_E$, $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell$ belongs to its maximal ideal $(t)$; hence $\ell^n\in(t^n)$ and $\ell^n A=0$. Since $\ell\ne p$, $\ell^n$ is invertible on every scheme under consideration. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so finite-type-over-Noetherian makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. Their open subschemes $U,V$ are Noetherian. Put $W=P\setminus i(U)$ and write $j:W\hookrightarrow P$. The affine presentation $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ shows that $P\to V$ is finite type. The opens $U,V$ are quasi-compact and their inclusions are quasi-compact: intersect with an affine open of their Noetherian targets and use quasi-compactness of a Noetherian open. Thus the quasi-compact-open finite-type theorem and composition show that $U,V,P$, and then $W$, are finite type over $k$; $W$ is Noetherian and $j$ is quasi-compact by the same argument. Closed immersions are proper, so $i$ is compactifiable by $(\mathrm{id},i)$; the intermediate separated finite-type maps admit compactifications by Nagata. Every ambient right adjoint used below therefore exists on the whole ordinary etale derived category. None is being formed by restriction to bounded constructible objects.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); coefficient and compactification hypotheses of the cited nodes

proof.text:
Use exact open extension on the ordinary etale categories. The first assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] gives $u_!\dashv u^*$ and $v_!\dashv v^*$ on the entire derived categories. For these open immersions its sum extension is the usual extension by zero, including the evaluation counit, by [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement]; applying its equality degreewise preserves that normalization. Let $F=Rf_{!,A}$ and $H=R\pi_{!,A}$. The unbounded compact-support composition comparisons and $fu=v\pi i$ give the specified natural isomorphism
$$\lambda:F u_!\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!H i_*.$$
Here compact support along an open $a$ is $a_!$ via $(a,\mathrm{id})$, with the source-open normalization of [lem-amb-compact-support-open-source-composition]. Compact support along the proper closed immersion $i$ is computed by the candidate $Ri_*$ of $(\mathrm{id},i)$. The closed immersion $i$ is separated, quasi-finite and of finite type between Noetherian schemes, so [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] gives a canonical isomorphism $c_i$ from every compactification candidate to the termwise exact functor $D(i^{\mathrm{supp}}_!)$ on the whole unbounded categories, compatible with the refinement comparisons. Here $i^{\mathrm{supp}}_!=i_*$: for etale $W\to P$ the support of a section over $U\times_PW$ is closed in $U\times_PW$, which is closed in $W$, hence proper over $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. This termwise $i_*$ is exactly the closed direct image of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] and [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. All these comparisons have unbounded domains.

The affine presentation of $P$ identifies $\pi$ with the trivial rank-$r$ vector bundle. Apply [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] over $V$: it identifies $\pi_A^\times$ with $G=\pi^*(-)(r)[2r]$ on all objects, and normalizes the adjunction $H\dashv G$ by the displayed integration counit, denoted $\epsilon^\pi$. Use $i_*\dashv Ri_A^!$ from [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. For arbitrary $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, take the following natural bijections:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,u^*f_A^\times L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(u_!M,f_A^\times L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Fu_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(v_!Hi_*M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_V(Hi_*M,v^*L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_P(i_*M,Gv^*L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,Ri_A^!Gv^*L).$$
In the third bijection a map $Fu_!M\to L$ is precomposed with $\lambda_M^{-1}$. Composition and uniqueness of right adjoints, with their pasted units and counits [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], identify the two representing functors. This gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha_L:u^*f_A^\times L\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_A^!(\pi^*v^*L(r)[2r])$. The Hom chain and purity apply before imposing any boundedness hypothesis on either $L$ or $f_A^\times L$.

source.place: Locality and Charts, expanded to a closed affine chart using unbounded vector-bundle purity

proof.text:
Make the counit assertion explicit. The left adjoint of the right side is $J=v_!Hi_*$ and its counit at $L$ is
$$e^J_L=\epsilon^v_L\circ v_!(\epsilon^\pi_{v^*L})\circ v_!H(\epsilon^i_{Gv^*L}).$$
The left adjoint of the left side is $Fu_!$ and its pasted counit is
$$e^{Fu}_L=\epsilon^f_L\circ F(\epsilon^u_{f_A^\times L}).$$
For $T_L=u^*f_A^\times L$, the Hom chain sends $1_{T_L}$ first to $\epsilon^u$, then to $e^{Fu}_L$, then to $e^{Fu}_L\circ\lambda_{T_L}^{-1}$, and finally to $\alpha_L$. Thus the inverse-transpose formula gives
$$e^J_L\circ J(\alpha_L)\circ\lambda_{T_L}=e^{Fu}_L.$$
This is exactly counit preservation relative to the specified compact-support composition comparison and the normalized purity counit. The same chain is natural in $L$ and $M$, so it specifies one natural transformation, not objectwise choices of isomorphisms. The pasted-counit formula is the one in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]; the purity counit is the transpose normalization in [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity].

source.place: Existence, uniqueness, naturality and Locality: expand the counit/transpose calculation

proof.text: Now let $L$ be bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Put $L'=\pi^*v^*L$. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image and its cohomology comparison give $\mathcal H^q(L')=\pi^*v^*\mathcal H^q(L)$, so the same cohomological bounds hold. Constructibility is preserved by [prop-constructible-pullback], applied to each cohomology sheaf (with the module-sheaf interpretation of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]). Apply the consequence for every scheme morphism in [lem-sf-etale-stalk-tor-test] first to $v$ and then to $\pi$: $L'$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. These assertions concern $L'$ directly; they use no preservation assertion for $f_A^\times$.

source.place: lemma-pullback-constructible; ordinary constant-coefficient pullback and the cited geometric-stalk Tor criterion

proof.text:
The ordinary Tate sheaf $B=A_P(r)$ is finite locally constant, flat and locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], with $N=\ell^n$. It is constructible: the single stratum $P$ and its finite locally constant sheaf satisfy the definition. The flat constructible tensor computation [lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor] makes $L'\otimes_A^L B$ bounded constructible. At every geometric point $\bar x$ choose a rank-one trivialization $B_{\bar x}\cong A$. The derived tensor/stalk comparison of [lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk] gives, for every $A$-module $Q$,
$$(L'\otimes_A^L B)_{\bar x}\otimes_A^LQ\cong L'_{\bar x}\otimes_A^LQ.$$
Hence the two directions of [lem-sf-etale-stalk-tor-test] preserve the same Tor interval. Put $K=(L'\otimes_A^LB)[2r]$. Since $\mathcal H^q(C[2r])=\mathcal H^{q+2r}(C)$, the shift makes $K$ bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a-2r,b-2r]$. This also covers $r=0$, for which $B=A_P$ and the shift is zero.

source.place: Affine-space paragraph: flat rank-one Tate twist; geometric-stalk verification of its Tor bound

proof.text: Obtain a bound for all module sheaves on the open complement, over the arbitrary field $k$ of the statement. Apply [lem-kun-uniform-field-extension-dimension-bound] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $W$: there is $d\geq0$ such that every field base change $W_L$ has dimension at most $d$. For any etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $W$, its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion, since $\ell^n$ kills all its sections. Apply [lem-kun-torsion-abelian-direct-image-dimension-bound] to the $k$-morphism $j:W\to P$. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite-type structure maps established in Step 1 and the just-chosen field-extension bound. Thus the abelian $R^qj_*$ vanishes for $q>2d$. The all-degree comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies this with the underlying abelian sheaf of the module $R^qj_*M$. A module sheaf whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero has only zero sections and is zero. Consequently $R^qj_*M=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and $q>c$, with $c=2d$. No separable-closedness or absolute cohomological-dimension hypothesis on $k$ has been inserted.

source.place: Tag 0F10 (lemma-finite-cd), arbitrary-field relative bound; cited field-extension dimension and coefficient-forgetting refinements

proof.text:
For a constructible $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $W$, apply [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] to $F[0]$ and $j:W\to P$. Both schemes are finite type over the same field $k$, and $A$ is finite and killed by the invertible integer $\ell^n$. It follows that every $R^qj_*F$ is constructible. Together with Step 7 this verifies both direct-image hypotheses of [prop-exc-closed-tor], with the quasi-compact complementary open $j$, the closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow P$, and the unchanged coefficient ring $\mathcal O_E/t^n$. Apply that theorem to the bounded constructible object $K$ from Step 6, with its Tor interval $[a-2r,b-2r]$. It gives $Ri_A^!K$ bounded constructible with Tor amplitude
$$[a-2r,b-2r+c+1].$$
This is the required expression and a finite interval. Steps 2–4 already established its identification with $u^*f_A^\times L$ for all $L$, independently of this preservation argument.
